root_cause.text: `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` in the BPF `PROG_ARRAY` map teardown path iterates over all entries and performs expensive `prog_array_map_poke_run()`/delete work per element without any rescheduling point, so large maps can monopolize CPU long enough to trigger RCU stalls under load.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cond_resched()` inside the `for (i = 0; i < array->map.max_entries; i++)` loop in `kernel/bpf/arraymap.c`, and the commit message explicitly says the loop calls `prog_array_map_poke_run()` per entry and “without yielding this can cause RCU stalls under load.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Yield the CPU while clearing BPF FD array maps to avoid long non-preemptible processing of large arrays.
intent_record.what: The loop in `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` was changed from a single-statement `for` loop to a braced block, and a `cond_resched()` call was inserted after each `__fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i, need_defer);` invocation.
intent_record.how: During clearing of a BPF FD array map, the function now voluntarily yields the CPU between element deletions, allowing the scheduler to run other tasks and preventing the operation from monopolizing the CPU for too long on large maps.

grouping_result.intent: Yield the CPU while clearing BPF FD array maps to avoid long non-preemptible processing of large arrays.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds CPU yielding during PROG_ARRAY/BPF FD array map clearing to prevent long uninterrupted teardown work and avoid RCU stalls on large maps.

candidates.rationale: This tight loop clears every entry in the PROG_ARRAY map without any rescheduling or yielding, which can monopolize CPU for a long time on large maps and contribute to RCU stalls.
This per-entry delete operation is executed repeatedly inside the unbounded teardown loop, and the expensive work done here is the direct source of the long non-preemptible processing.

vuln_statements.explanation: This teardown loop iterates over every PROG_ARRAY entry with no rescheduling point, enabling long CPU monopolization during map clearing and contributing to RCU stalls.
This per-element delete work is executed for each entry in the tight teardown loop, and its repeated expensive processing is part of the long non-preemptible section that can trigger RCU stalls.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet contains the teardown/clear path for PROG_ARRAY maps: `void bpf_prog_array_map_clear(struct bpf_map *map)` iterates `for (i = 0; i < array->map.max_entries; i++) prog_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i);`. This is exactly the kind of full-map per-entry deletion loop described in the root cause, and there is no rescheduling point, batching, or other mitigation in the loop. The delete helper itself also does per-element work via `xchg(array->prog + index, NULL)` and `bpf_prog_put(old_prog)`. The fix is not present here because nothing breaks up the loop or yields CPU.

    Both map deletion operation, map release and map free operation use

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is an unconditional teardown loop in `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` that calls the expensive delete path for every entry without a special-case fix for map-free teardown. In this snippet, that logic is already changed: `bpf_fd_array_map_clear` now takes a `bool need_defer`, and the map-free callers pass `false` (`bpf_fd_array_map_clear(map, false);` in `perf_event_fd_array_map_free()`, `cgroup_fd_array_free()`, and `array_of_map_free()`). The per-element delete helper was also split so it can avoid deferred work: `__fd_array_map_delete_elem(map, key, need_defer)` and `map->ops->map_fd_put_ptr(map, old_ptr, need_defer);`. The old unconditional behavior is still used only via the wrapper `fd_array_map_delete_elem(..., true)` for deletion/release paths, which matches the commit message. Therefore the bug is not present in this commit and the fix is already included.
